sourceEnglishObjective: Warn about slippery conditions and changing weather
sourceEnglishSpeaking: Warn the crew about slick footing and bring them down when lightning approaches.
candidateObjective: 滑りやすい状態と変わる天候について警告する。
candidateFocus: ～ので gives the reason for a warning. ～たら sets a weather-change condition; ～てください gives a direct instruction to come down.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 嵐が近づいています。今すぐ降りてください。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: A storm is coming. Come down now.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 天候が変わったら作業を止めて降りてください。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Stop work and come down if the weather changes.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 滑りにくい作業靴を履いてください。
朝露で滑りやすいので、安定した足元を探します。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: We look for solid footing because the dew is slick.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 天候が変わったら降りてください。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Come down if the weather changes.

archivedSpeaking.opening: 屋根が朝露で滑りやすくなっています。足元に気をつけてください。嵐が近づいているので、今すぐ降りてください。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Warn the crew about slick footing and bring them down when lightning approaches.

curriculumAdaptationNote: Preserve the current source sequence: at 6:30 dew remains on the roof; foreman warns the roof is wet; crew seeks solid footing and wears grip boots; later wind rises and dark clouds appear; source prohibits roof work in lightning; foreman calls for immediate descent as a storm approaches; final line says stop and come down if weather changes. The source's broad weather-change trigger, roof work on dew and footwear claims require qualified roofing/weather safety review. The speaking objective explicitly says bring crew down when lightning approaches, while archived speaking opening mentions only an approaching storm; keep those cues coherent. Archived 雷 can mean thunder or lightning and 作業靴 is broader than boots. Current curriculum has no authored verb-example list; archived forms remain conditional evidence. No selected learner/audio text or progress identity is created.

cards.reviewNote: Footing / apoyo firme al pisar is secure placement and traction while stepping, not merely 足元の安定 as an abstract state. Confirm a natural Japanese term and the roof-work safety context.
雷 may denote thunder or lightning; source specifically means electrical lightning hazard. Confirm Japanese term and timing with qualified safety/Japanese review.
Boots / botas is footwear type, while archived 作業靴 covers work shoes broadly. Keep boot sense and grip-property claims distinct.

cards.sourceSpanish: Cuidado al pisar — el rocío resbala.
cards.sourceEnglish: Watch your footing — the dew is slick.
cards.candidateJapanese: 足元に気をつけてください。朝露で滑りやすくなっています。
cards.archivedJapanese: 足元に気をつけてください。朝露で滑りやすくなっています。
cards.archivedEnglish: Watch your footing — the dew is slick.

cards.sourceSpanish: No trabajen el techo con relámpagos.
cards.sourceEnglish: Don't work the roof in lightning.
cards.archivedJapanese: 雷が発生している間は屋根で作業しないでください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Don't work the roof in lightning.
cards.reviewNote: The source prohibits roof work in lightning. Archived 雷が発生している間 can read as only while lightning is actively occurring; settle onset/approach and safe-stop timing before scoring.

cards.sourceSpanish: Detengan el trabajo y bajen si cambia el tiempo.
cards.sourceEnglish: Stop work and come down if the weather changes.
cards.archivedJapanese: 天候が変わったら作業を止めて降りてください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Stop work and come down if the weather changes.
cards.reviewNote: Source says stop work and come down if weather changes. This broadly worded trigger needs qualified roofing/weather safety context; archived Japanese should not imply every harmless change or wait past lightning approach.

cards.sourceSpanish: El techo está mojado. Tengan cuidado.
cards.sourceEnglish: The roof is wet. Be careful.
cards.candidateJapanese: 屋根が濡れています。気をつけてください。
cards.archivedJapanese: 屋根が濡れています。気をつけてください。
cards.archivedEnglish: The roof is wet. Be careful.

cards.sourceEnglish: A storm is coming. Come down now.
cards.archivedJapanese: 嵐が近づいています。今すぐ降りてください。
cards.archivedEnglish: A storm is coming. Come down now.
cards.reviewNote: Source commands immediate descent for an approaching storm. Confirm timing, roof-exit sequence and lightning approach consistency with the speaking objective; do not treat isolated sentence as a complete emergency procedure.

cards.archivedJapanese: 滑りにくい作業靴を履いてください。
cards.reviewNote: Source specifies boots with good grip. Archived 滑りにくい作業靴 loses boots; qualified reviewer must ensure footwear is not presented as sufficient control for a wet roof.

reader.archivedJapanese: 午前六時半、屋根にはまだ朝露が残っています。
reader.archivedEnglish: It is 6:30 in the morning and there is still dew on the roof.

reader.sourceSpanish: El capataz advierte: El techo está mojado. Tengan cuidado.
reader.sourceEnglish: The foreman warns: The roof is wet. Be careful.
reader.candidateJapanese: 職長は「屋根が濡れています。気をつけてください」と警告します。
reader.archivedJapanese: 職長は「屋根が濡れています。気をつけてください」と警告します。

reader.sourceSpanish: Busquen un apoyo firme al pisar, porque el rocío hace resbaloso el techo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Look for solid footing, because the dew makes the roof slippery.
reader.archivedJapanese: 朝露で屋根が滑りやすいため、安定した足元を探してください。
reader.archivedEnglish: Look for solid footing, because the dew makes the roof slippery.
reader.reviewNote: Look for solid footing on a dew-slick roof is source text, not a complete safe-work method. Confirm 足元 and 安定した足元 language and safety sequence before learner-facing instructions.

reader.archivedJapanese: 滑りにくい作業靴を履いてください。
reader.reviewNote: Source says boots with good grip; archived 作業靴 is broader work shoes, and footwear alone does not resolve wet-roof hazard.

reader.archivedJapanese: その後、風が強まり、空に暗い雲が現れます。

reader.reviewNote: Do not work the roof in lightning; confirm Japanese 雷 sense and stop/evacuation timing before scoring or audio.

reader.sourceSpanish: El capataz grita: Viene una tormenta. Bajen ahora.
reader.sourceEnglish: The foreman shouts: A storm is coming. Come down now.
reader.archivedJapanese: 職長は「嵐が近づいています。今すぐ降りてください」と叫びます。
reader.archivedEnglish: The foreman shouts: A storm is coming. Come down now.
reader.reviewNote: Storm coming / come down now must be coordinated with the speaking objective's lightning approach, not delayed until visible lightning or a storm already arrives.

reader.sourceSpanish: Detengan el trabajo y bajen si cambia el tiempo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Stop work and come down if the weather changes.

reader.archivedEnglish: Stop work and come down if the weather changes.
reader.reviewNote: Broad 'if weather changes' trigger needs qualified safety context and must not weaken the immediate storm/lightning instruction in Reader 7.
